extracted.intended_audience: registrants (issuers) preparing SEC filings, corporate accountants, and auditors advising on business combination reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on performing the SEC 'income' and 'revenue' tests of significance for business combinations (S‑X rules), including calculation of pretax income and revenue components, treatment of NCI, losses, averaging, aggregate tests, and special situations (e.g., fair value option).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretax income component formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant’s share of the acquired business’s pretax income ÷ Registrant’s consolidated pretax income. This formula is applied using absolute values, meaning a pretax loss from continuing operations is a positive number in the calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pretax income for purposes of this test is income from continuing operations before income taxes. The result of the pretax income component is used (along with the revenue component, if applicable) to determine significance under the income test (the lower of the two results). [S‑X Rule 1‑02(w)(1)(iii)(A)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretax income numerator — what to include
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant’s share of the acquired business’s pretax income includes direct and indirect ownership interests. Pretax income is income from continuing operations before income taxes, but after (a) eliminating transactions between the registrant and the acquired business, and (b) attributing amounts to the acquired business’s noncontrolling interest (NCI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pretax income cannot be adjusted for nonrecurring or special charges or credits. See related Q&A on eliminating intercompany transactions and attributing NCI. (Refs: Questions 3.3.190, 3.3.100)

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretax income denominator — registrant consolidated pretax income
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant’s consolidated pretax income is income from continuing operations before taxes, excluding the income of the acquired business, after (a) eliminating transactions between the registrant and the acquired business, and (b) attributing amounts to the registrant’s NCI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Like the numerator, the registrant’s pretax income cannot be adjusted for nonrecurring or special charges or credits. If the revenue component does not apply and the modified denominator conditions are met, a five‑year average may be used as the denominator. [S‑X Rule 1‑02(w)(1)(iii)(B)(2)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified denominator (five‑year averaging) rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A modified denominator (the average of the absolute values of the registrant’s income or loss from continuing operations for the last five years) is used if: (1) the revenue component does not apply, and (2) the absolute value of the registrant’s consolidated pretax income (or loss) for the most recent fiscal year is at least 10% lower than the average of the absolute values for the last five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is known as the modified denominator. Income averaging of the acquired business is not permitted — averaging applies only to the registrant’s results. See examples illustrating when to use the five‑year average. [S‑X Rule 1‑02(w)(1)(iii)(B)(2); FRM 2015.8]

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of registrant’s share when NCI exists or partial acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant acquires 100% of a business and the acquired business presents NCI, the registrant uses the pretax income (or revenue) attributable to controlling interest as reported on the acquired business’s financial statements. If a registrant acquires less than 100% of a business, the numerator is the acquired business’s pretax income (or revenue) (or pretax income attributable to controlling interest if the acquired business has its own NCI) multiplied by the percentage of the business acquired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This method also applies if a registrant’s consolidated, but less‑than‑wholly‑owned subsidiary acquires 100% of a business. Guidance parallels the asset and revenue tests. [Regs Comm 03/2022]

rubrics_metrics.name: Include direct and indirect ownership interests in numerator
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant’s proportionate share of the acquired business’s pretax income (and revenue) includes both direct and indirect ownership interests — indirect ownership is converted to the registrant’s effective interest by multiplying intermediate ownership percentages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate combining a registrant’s direct purchase with amounts acquired indirectly through a subsidiary (e.g., direct ownership plus indirect ownership × parent ownership).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of pretax losses — absolute value rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant, the acquired business, or both have a pretax loss rather than income, the absolute value of the pretax loss is used to determine the pretax income component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When performing the test, treat losses as positive (absolute) numbers. If the revenue component does not apply for lack of material revenue, registrant might have to use the five‑year average of absolute pretax income/loss. [S‑X Rule 1‑02(w)(1)(iii)(A)(1)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate significance testing — cannot offset losses and incomes
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining aggregate significance for individually insignificant acquisitions, a registrant cannot offset pretax losses of one or more individually insignificant acquired businesses with pretax income of other individually insignificant acquired businesses, nor aggregate the absolute values of pretax income and losses of the individually insignificant businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant must perform two separate significance tests — one for the group with pretax losses and one for the group with pretax income. If the significance of either group exceeds 50%, the pretax income component is met for the entire pool of individually insignificant acquired businesses (not just the entities in the single group that exceeded 50%). [S‑X Rule 1‑02(w)(1)(iii)(B)(3); S‑X Rule 3‑05(b)(2)(iv)]

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretax income component in acquisition of equity investment when fair value option elected
rubrics_metrics.description: For an equity investment that will be accounted for using the fair value option, the pretax income component should be performed using the change in fair value of the relevant instrument (e.g., common stock) during the applicable historical period (usually the most recently completed pre‑acquisition fiscal year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant also performs the revenue component if both investor and investee have material recurring annual revenue in each of the two most recently completed fiscal years. No adjustments are made to the revenue component due to election of the fair value option. [2021 AICPA Conf; Regs Comm 03/2011]

rubrics_metrics.name: Revenue component formula and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Revenue component = Registrant’s share of the acquired business’s consolidated total revenue ÷ Registrant’s consolidated total revenue (for the most recently completed fiscal year). The revenue component does not apply if either the registrant or the acquired business does not have material revenue in each of the two most recently completed fiscal years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the revenue component does not apply, perform only the pretax income component. The income test result is the lesser of the pretax income and revenue component results (if revenue applies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Material revenue determination
rubrics_metrics.description: No specific threshold exists for determining if the registrant and acquired business have 'material revenue'; judgment is necessary and both quantitative and qualitative factors should be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC staff has indicated that whether a registrant or acquired business has material revenue should be readily apparent and does not require an analysis under SAB Topic 1.M (SAB 99). The SEC staff encourages registrants to consult with it if uncertain. [2020 AICPA Conf]

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant’s share of revenue when NCI present or partial acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant acquires 100% of a business and that business has consolidated subsidiaries with NCI, use the revenue as reported on the acquired business’s financial statements (no adjustment for the NCI holder’s interest). If a registrant acquires less than 100% of a business, the numerator is the acquired business’s revenue multiplied by the percentage acquired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, if a registrant’s consolidated but less‑than‑wholly‑owned subsidiary acquires 100% of a business, use the acquired business’s reported revenue without adjustment for the NCI holder’s interest. [Regs Comm 03/2022]

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate revenue component for individually insignificant acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: For pools of individually insignificant acquisitions, separate the pool into pretax income and pretax loss groups. If a group (income or loss) had material combined revenue (and the registrant had material revenue) for the last two fiscal years, the revenue component for that group is performed based on the group’s aggregate revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is possible the revenue component applies to one group but not the other. If either group's lower‑of‑components (or pretax income component if revenue doesn't apply) is greater than 50%, the entire pool of individually insignificant acquired businesses is significant under the income test. Examples illustrate computing aggregate revenue and individual significances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate revenue component for related businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple acquired businesses are related under S‑X Rule 3‑05(a)(3), combine the revenues of the related businesses as if they were a single business for purposes of the revenue component of the income test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance for related businesses is not determined individually or by separating into pretax income and pretax loss groups. If the combined revenue for related businesses is not material for each of the last two years, the revenue component does not apply. [FRM 2020.10; 2020 AICPA Conf]
